Thought: Let me analyze each option to determine how azo compounds are formed:

A. Detonation of inorganic azides - Inorganic azides typically decompose to release nitrogen gas when detonated, but this is not how azo compounds (which contain -N=N- linkage) are formed.

B. Oxidation of substituted hydrazines - Hydrazines have an N-N single bond structure (H₂N-NH₂), and oxidation of substituted hydrazines can convert this single bond to a double bond, forming the characteristic -N=N- linkage of azo compounds.

C. Reaction of sodium azide with alkyl sulfates - This reaction typically forms organic azides (R-N₃), not azo compounds.

D. Reduction of primary amines - Reduction of primary amines typically leads to compounds with lower oxidation states, not azo compounds which require formation of N=N bonds.

Based on my analysis, azo compounds are formed by the oxidation of substituted hydrazines, which converts the N-N single bond to the N=N double bond characteristic of azo compounds.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
